principles: API signatures should expose real data dependencies.
A maintenance refactor must preserve observable behaviour.
Verification effort should be proportional but mechanically recorded.
drivers: The unused parameter falsely implies prior-state-dependent reset logic.
The helper and all callers are internal.
Existing smoke assertions already encode the intended reset contract.
rationale: The reset is intentionally derived only from current counters, and the handler independently keeps prior state for authorization and audit text. Removing the parameter is the smallest honest representation of the contract.

preMortem.trigger: TypeScript compilation reports an argument-count mismatch or rg finds a two-argument call
preMortem.consequence: Build fails or misleading usage remains
preMortem.mitigation: Use rg before and after editing, then run the package build.

preMortem.trigger: Focused smoke fails baseline, frozen, or recovery-budget assertions
preMortem.consequence: Human ack no longer opens a fresh convergence window
preMortem.mitigation: Change only the signature/calls and run convergence-breaker-smoke.

preMortem.trigger: A phase gate repeatedly requests evidence already recorded at the same HEAD
preMortem.consequence: A trivial refactor enters an assurance loop
preMortem.mitigation: Follow each gate hint once, capture exact blocker output, and avoid self-classifying freshness.
